chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who falls ill and Ramadan overtakes him while he is ill and does not recover until another Ramadan overtakes him, he said: He gives charity for the first [year] and fasts the second [year]. And if he recovered in between but did not fast until another Ramadan overtook him, he fasts both [years] and gives charity for the first [year].
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed Ramadan fasts if illness extends until the next Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between prolonged illness and temporary incapacity, establishing that continuous sickness until the next Ramadan requires both Qada (making up fasts) and Fidya (charity), whereas intermittent recovery mandates only Qada. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the severity of delaying obligatory acts, linking the missed fasts to the charity of the previous year to emphasize accountability. The ruling underscores the practical implication that health status at the onset of the new Ramadan determines the cumulative obligations for the preceding year.
